paper_title: PBT-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Property-Based Testing
reason: 저장된 초안을 재개할 수 없어 보류했습니다. 재감사(reaudit) 요청이 필요합니다: The official card mentions the evaluation harness; cite it instead of claiming absence

row.정의: 실제 Python 라이브러리 40개에서 속성 기반 테스트(PBT) 문제 100개를 선별한 벤치마크. 문제마다 의미적 버그가 하나 이상 주입돼 있으며 총 365개(문제당 평균 3.65개)이고 난이도는 L1 87개, L2 184개, L3 94개이다. 에이전트는 문서만 오라클로 삼아 불변식을 찾고 Hypothesis @given 전략으로 버그를 드러내야 한다. 버그별로 '버그 버전에서는 실패하고 수정 버전에서는 통과'하는지로 채점하며 지표는 bug recall, 문제 커버리지(F≥1), 전체 회수(Perfect)이다. 논문은 모델 8종을 두 가지 프롬프트(개방형 baseline, Hypothesis 스캐폴딩)로 설정당 3회 평가했다.
row.대표 과제: 문서를 읽고 불변식을 도출해 Hypothesis 속성 테스트(pbt_test.py)를 작성하고, 주입된 버그별 fail-to-pass 여부로 채점
row.대표 예시·설명: 버그가 주입된 Python 라이브러리와 문서(docs/)가 주어지면, 에이전트가 문서에서 읽은 불변식을 @given 전략으로 표현해 버그가 발동하는 드문 입력 영역까지 무작위 탐색하는 테스트를 작성하는 과제 설명(실제 문항 아님)
row.이용 시 유의사항: 라이선스, 상업적 이용, 수정·파생, 재배포, lm-eval 지원은 아직 확인하지 않았다. 문제에 쓰인 라이브러리와 문서는 제3자 저작물이므로 각 구성 요소의 약관을 이용 전에 따로 확인해야 한다. 문제 파일에 BIG-bench canary 문자열이 들어 있어 학습 데이터에 넣지 않도록 주의해야 한다. 실행에는 컨테이너(Docker 또는 Apptainer) 환경과 에이전트 하니스(OpenHands SDK)가 필요하다. 의도적으로 주입한 버그라 실제 소프트웨어 버그 분포를 대표하지는 않는다. 논문 수치는 해당 논문 조건의 결과이며 현재 전역 리더보드가 아니다.

english_copy.definition: PBT-Bench is a benchmark of 100 curated property-based testing (PBT) problems across 40 real Python libraries. Each problem injects one or more semantic bugs (365 in total, mean 3.65 per problem), labelled L1 (87), L2 (184), and L3 (94). Using only the documentation as the oracle, an agent must identify an invariant and write a Hypothesis @given strategy that exposes the bug. Each bug is scored by whether a test fails on the buggy version and passes on the version with that bug reversed. Metrics are bug recall, problem coverage (F≥1), and full recall (Perfect). The paper evaluates eight models under two prompting regimes (open-ended baseline and Hypothesis scaffolding) with three runs per configuration.
english_copy.task: Read the documentation, derive invariants, write Hypothesis property tests (pbt_test.py), and be scored per injected bug by fail-to-pass.
english_copy.example: Task description (not an actual test item): given a buggy Python library and its documentation, the agent expresses a documented invariant as a @given strategy that reaches the rare input region where the bug triggers.

screening.paper_title: PBT-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Property-Based Testing
screening.abstract: Existing code benchmarks measure whether an agent can produce any test that reproduces a known bug, or whether it can produce a patch that fixes a described issue. Neither isolates the distinct skill of property-based testing: deriving a semantic invariant from documentation, and then constructing an input-generation strategy precise enough to make a random search reveal the violation. We introduce PBT-Bench, a benchmark of 100 curated property-based testing problems across 40 real Python libraries. Each problem injects one or more semantic bugs (365 in total, mean 3.65 per problem) designed so that default-strategy random inputs almost never trigger them; the agent must read the library's documentation, identify the relevant invariant, and specify a Hypothesis @given strategy that concentrates mass in the trigger region. Bugs are stratified across three difficulty levels (L1-L3) spanning single-constraint boundary bugs to stateful, cross-function protocol violations. We evaluate eight contemporary LLMs under two prompting regimes (open-ended baseline vs. explicit Hypothesis scaffolding) for three independent runs per configuration. Bug recall under the PBT-guided prompt ranges from 42.1% to 83.4% across models; under the open-ended baseline, from 31.4% to 76.7%. Hypothesis scaffolding lifts mid-capability models by over 20 percentage points, but yields smaller gains for the strongest models, with two exceptions showing degradation, suggesting the structured prompt can interfere with certain model behaviours rather than complementing them. The hardest bugs prove model-specific: different architectures fail on different problems, leaving persistent gaps that no single model closes. We release the benchmark, harness, and full evaluation corpus to support downstream work on documentation-grounded semantic reasoning.
